title: What is man?
hook: when I consider the heavens, what is man, that thou art mindful of him? (Psalm 8)
tomorrow: what did a shepherd boy fight off to save one lamb?

segments.voice: Yesterday, by the rivers: the tree in Psalm 1, strong because of where its roots reach. Today the psalm looks up, all the way up.

A bad week at work can make a person feel replaceable. Then a step outside at night, under an enormous sky, can make a person feel smaller still. How small is one person under all those stars? Psalm 8 asks it out loud, in the King James Version: "When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained; What is man, that thou art mindful of him?"
screen: `A WEEK THAT MAKES YOU FEEL REPLACEABLE.` → `THE SKY IS ENORMOUS.` → `WHAT IS MAN?`

segments.voice: The psalm doesn't leave the question hanging. The next line answers: "For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour." Small under the stars, and crowned. Matthew tells a day when Jesus used this psalm. In the Temple in Jerusalem, children are shouting Hosanna to the Son of David. The chief priests and scribes are indignant: do you hear what these are saying? Jesus answers from Psalm 8: "Yea; have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise?" The smallest voices in the courtyard, and the psalm says they count. Readers hear Genesis in this psalm, where God makes humankind in his own image. That's the root of a belief Jews and Christians share: every human being has worth, a dignity no job title gives and no bad week takes away. In that belief, the stars don't shrink it. They're the backdrop it's measured against.
screen: `A LITTLE LOWER THAN THE ANGELS.` · `CHILDREN SHOUTING IN THE TEMPLE.` · `OUT OF THE MOUTH OF BABES.` · `MADE IN GOD'S IMAGE.` · then, large: `WHAT IS MAN.`

segments.voice: If you can, look at the sky: the moon, a few stars, or just the dark or the clouds through a window. Let it be as big as it is. Then rest your attention on your own breath for the rest of the sit, one small life, still breathing under all of it.
What is man? Psalm 8's question under the stars, and its answer: a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory.
Hold on to this: what is man, small under the sky and still crowned. Two psalms read, and the sky got bigger.

howItsDone: Jews and Christians pray Psalm 8 as a psalm of praise; both traditions teach that every human being is made in the image of God, a belief often grounded in Genesis 1 and Psalm 8.
